transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-04
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~55 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Mark Davies (Stonybrook - Head of ML), Sara Lopez (Stonybrook - Infra Lead), Tom Reed (Stonybrook - Procurement)

Auto-summary (auto): Stonybrook is evaluating Redwood Dedicated for reserved GPU capacity. Needs: tenant isolation, VPC/private deployment options, burst for nightly batch/ETL, predictable unit economics, SOC2 and KMS integration. They want a pilot to run benchmarks against current on-prem cluster.

Topics: sizing, burst policy, VPC/Private, SOC2/KMS, latency SLAs, pricing, procurement timeline

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex (Redwood): Hey everyone thanks for joining, I'm Alex Chen from Redwood, with Priya our SE. How's every- one doing?
[00:06] Mark (Customer): Doing well thanks Alex. Excited to dig in. We've been looking at dedicated capacity options — we want isolated GPUs for some of our gen-AI models.
[00:12] Priya (Redwood): Great. Can you give a quick picture of your current infra and workload patterns?
[00:18] Mark: Sure. We run a mix — low-latency online scoring for customer support and higher-throughput nightly batch runs for retraining and document embeddings. Online is pretty latency-sensitive, target 100-200 ms 95th for small prompts. Nightly jobs are huge, tens of thousands of docs, we want to burst into extra GPUs to finish in a window.
[00:35] Sara: And from infra side, everything is behind our VPC. Some model training is on-prem, others on AWS. We need isolation — customer data cannot touch shared tenants. SOC2 and encryption in transit and at rest are must-haves.
[00:48] Alex: Totally understood. Redwood Dedicated is built for reserved pools and VPC peering or Private deployments. For strict isolation we'd recommend dedicated pools with VPC peering or our Private control plane depending on your compliance needs.
[00:59] Tom: Quick Q from procurement — what does the contract cadence look like? Annual commit? Monthly? How flexible is burst pricing?
[01:05] Alex: Typical is reserved monthly/annual commits for baseline capacity; burst can be configured as pay-as-you-go with controls. We'll send a sizing/pricing sheet but you can do a baseline commit to keep predictability and allow burst to cover peaks.
[01:18] Mark: How seamless is fallback to hosted models if dedicated runs out? We like graceful degradation — keep service up.
[01:24] Priya: We have smart routing and fallback policies. If Dedicated capacity maxes out, requests can fall back to hosted variants or cheaper quantized replicas, based on policy. You can set priorities per route. There's also automatic throttling so SLAs degrade gracefully.
[01:38] Mark: Nice. A few technical specifics — do you support KV cache and session reuse for chat workloads?
[01:42] Priya: Yes, KV cache and prefix caching are supported; we can pin models and manage KV cache within the runtime. That reduces tokens and helps latency for repeated sessions.
[01:50] Sara: Ok but networking, for Private option — do you require an outbound connection to Redwood control plane? We are strict about egress.
[01:56] Alex: For Redwood Private we can do a customer-hosted control plane option — on-prem package is available for air-gapped setups. For VPC deployments we typically have a control plane with limited outbound; we can discuss firewall rules and proxy setups. We'll get our security docs over.
[02:12] Tom: Procurement also needs compliance paperwork — SOC2, iso, and any pen-test reports.
[02:17] Alex: Yes we'll share SOC2 and our compliance pack. We'll include KMS/HSM integrations notes — many customers integrate their cloud KMS or an HSM.
[02:25] Mark: What about autoscaling behavior? We want baseline low latency for online plus the ability to spin up for nightly batches. Ideally the baseline is 4 GPUs and burst to 12 for a few hours. How fast can you scale?
[02:35] Priya: Scaling depends on mode. With Dedicated reserved pools we can do fast scaling within your reserved capacity. For burst beyond reserved, we use queued provisioning; typically minutes for warm ready nodes, quicker if you have burst capacity pre-warmed. We also recommend pre-warming burst capacity for nightly windows to hit SLA.
[02:50] Mark: Any recommendations on model quantization? We're running some 70B models today.
[02:54] Priya: Quantization is a big lever. We can run 70B in int8/4 quant modes depending on tolerance for quality. Redwood Optimize will suggest quantization profiles per workload; we can run a quality/regression eval as part of the POC.
[03:06] Sara: For the POC, we'll need to run our own payloads. Are there data residency concerns? We need logs kept in our environment, and long-term retention options.
[03:15] Alex: Logs and audit trails can be routed to your SIEM and kept per retention you choose if you're on Dedicated/Private. Hosted customers have configurable retention tiers, but Dedicated gives you better control.
[03:26] Tom: Rough timeline — we want procurement done in 3-4 weeks if POC looks good. Who will be the Redwood contact for procurement?
[03:33] Alex: I'll own the deal and liaise with your procurement. Priya will lead the technical POC.
[03:38] Mark: Benchmarks — we want latency numbers for online 95th and throughput for batch. Can you run a benchmark against our sample payloads?
[03:44] Priya: Absolutely. We'll need sample payloads, typical prompt shapes, and concurrency targets. We'll then run both quant and fp16 variants and share token-level latency and cost breakdowns.
[03:55] Mark: Cool. One concern — vendor lock-in. If we wanted to move models or run hybrid, how portable is the config and runtime?
[04:01] Priya: We expose a consistent API and model pinning. You can export configs, and the runtime supports standard model formats. The idea is portability across hosted/dedicated/private with the same API layer.
[04:11] Sara: Are there bandwidth egress costs we should expect when moving large model checkpoints?
[04:15] Alex: Checkpoint uploads typically incur cloud egress on your side; for Private/on-prem it's internal. We can advise best practices — use incremental syncs, or bring-your-own-image for large models. We'll document this in the runbook.
[04:26] Mark: Anything about monitoring and tracing? We need per-route dashboards and token cost breakdowns.
[04:30] Priya: Redwood Console provides per-route metrics, token-level cost, tracing hooks, and alerting. For Dedicated we can forward telemetry into your observability stack as well.
[04:39] Tom: From procurement perspective, what's the minimum commitment?
[04:43] Alex: There's a baseline recommended minimum for Dedicated — typically a 3- or 6-month minimum for initial reserved capacity, but we can be flexible depending on POC. We'll put options in the pricing sheet.
[04:52] Mark: Ok. For the pilot we'd like to validate: 1) online 95th latency meeting 100-200ms, 2) batch throughput to finish nightly within 4 hours, 3) no data exposure and SOC2 alignment. That's our success criteria.
[05:02] Priya: Sounds good. We'll scope the POC with those acceptance criteria.
[05:06] Alex: Great. I'll send the pricing and sizing and Priya will reach out to schedule the benchmark. Sara, can you share the VPC diagram and compliance contact?
[05:13] Sara: Yes, I'll send that after this call.
[05:16] Tom: We'll also share procurement windows.
[05:18] Alex: Perfect. Any final questions?
[05:21] Mark: One small thing — can you share a sample SLA for Dedicated latency targets?
[05:25] Alex: Yes, we'll attach our SLA doc.
[05:27] Priya: Also share any model/quantization recommendations we run during POC.
[05:30] Mark: Great.
[05:31] Alex: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the docs.
[05:34] (call ends)
